name: Nas
hook: A Queensbridge teenager whose first album gathered the best producers in New York on one record, each doing their best work for him.
blurb: Nasir Jones grew up in the Queensbridge housing projects, the same place Marley Marl's Juice Crew came from. His father, Olu Dara, is a jazz cornet player. Large Professor put him on a Main Source record in 1991, when he was seventeen. His first album, Illmatic, came out in 1994. It had only ten songs, but they were produced by five of the best beat-makers of the time, most of them already on this map: Large Professor, DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip and L.E.S., and several of the tracks are among the best-known work each of them did. It is the clearest case on the map of producers as their own line of influence, separate from the artists. That the record belongs to a rapper rather than a producer is part of the point: by 1994 a label gathered producers the way Sugar Hill once gathered a house band.
